resources.string: Choose Create New Project, enter a name, pick Empty, Office, Residential or Data center, then choose display units. Templates provide a starting level, drawing layers and room footprints. The drawing canvas opens after creation. Project details lets you change the name, description and units.

Open Tools and choose a shape. Choosing a drawing tool opens the 2D plan; picked points lie on the selected level’s XY plane. Line takes two endpoints; rectangle takes opposite corners. Circle takes a centre and radius point; ellipse takes a centre and a corner defining its horizontal and vertical radii. Arc takes a start, a point on the arc, then an end. Triangle takes three corners. For a polyline, polygon or spline, tap the points and choose Finish. Closed polyline needs at least three points. Cancel discards the unfinished shape. Collapse Tools at any time to make room for drawing.

For Text, enter the lettering and its height in Tools, then tap its insertion point. For Leader, enter the text, tap its arrow point and bends, then Finish. An aligned dimension takes two measured endpoints and a third point for the dimension line. Angular takes the vertex, first arm, second arm, then label position. Radial takes the centre, radius point, then label position. Dimensions measure their stored anchors; moving another object does not move a dimension’s anchors automatically.

Box and pyramid take two opposite base corners. Sphere, cylinder and cone take a centre and radius point. Set Height in Tools for box, pyramid, cylinder or cone before picking points. The base is on the selected level plane; height extends upward. Switch to 3D to orbit the new wireframe object. A sphere extends above and below its centre.

Choose Select, then tap an object. Enable Add selection to toggle objects into or out of a multiple selection. Dragging an object’s body pans or orbits the camera. Transform only with the on-screen handles: arrows move along their axes, the ring rotates about Z, and the square scales uniformly. In plan view, use X and Y handles; orbit view also offers Z when visible. Properties edits one object’s numeric X, Y, Z, rotation about each axis in degrees, and local width, depth and height in the project units. Flat axes cannot gain thickness. Apply commits the changes; Cancel leaves the object as it was.

With a selection, use Copy and Paste, Mirror X or Mirror Y, Array, or Delete in Tools. Arrays include the original cell, allow negative X/Y spacing, and accept 2–1,000 cells with up to 100 rows and columns; a repeated axis needs nonzero spacing. An array is one undo step. Undo and Redo apply to the current editing session, up to the history size in Settings. Reopening a project starts a new history and clipboard. Save keeps the drawing, including its edits; undo history is not restored after process death.

Save writes your project to the local library on this device. Export creates a portable .eezydraw file in a location you choose. If you select a save folder in Settings, the app also writes project copies there; the local library stays available on this device.

Continue Project opens the most recent project. Select a recent-project thumbnail to open that project instead. Open from file imports a .eezydraw file into your local library. Existing local projects are not silently overwritten by imported files.

Settings controls defaults for newly created projects. Changing a project’s display units does not rescale its geometry: stored lengths stay in metres. Existing projects keep their own units and project settings. Theme, input mode and other app preferences are stored separately from project files.

Choose an autosave interval in Settings, or switch it off. Save important changes before leaving a project. With backups enabled, saving retains the preceding saved version. If a project cannot be read, use the offered backup recovery action to restore an available earlier version.
Open a project, expand Tools, and choose a drawing or selection tool. Tap to pick points or objects; use the transform handles to edit a selection.

Tap a card or button to open it. Swipe vertically to scroll forms and recent projects. Tap a text field to edit it. Use the back arrow or Android Back to return; save any changes before leaving a project.

In 2D, drag with one finger to pan and pinch to zoom. With a drawing tool, tap to add snapped points; Finish completes a polyline, polygon, spline or leader. With Select, tap an object; Add selection toggles multiple objects. Drag arrows to move, the ring to rotate, or the square to scale. Dragging an object’s body moves the camera. Snap probe tracks points without panning. In 3D, drag to orbit or use two fingers to pan and zoom. View cube faces and view presets align the camera. Zoom window fits a dragged rectangle; Zoom extents fits the visible drawing.

On the canvas, use Ctrl+C to copy, Ctrl+V to paste, Ctrl+Z to undo, Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y to redo, and Delete to remove the selection. Escape cancels an unfinished drawing operation or clears selection. Use Tab to move between controls, Enter or Space to activate a focused button, and Android Back to return. TalkBack announces labelled controls and transform-handle actions. Keyboard editing shortcuts apply when the canvas has focus; text fields keep their normal editing behavior.

EEZY DRAW is a tablet-first MEP drawing application. This version includes project creation, a local library, portable project files, settings, help, plan and orbit wireframe views, shape and annotation tools, 3D primitives, selection, transforms and session undo/redo. Coordination engines and external CAD file codecs remain separate development stages.

The project library works offline. Exports and save-folder copies go only to the locations you choose. Uninstalling the app removes its private library; keep exported copies of important projects. Feedback does not attach project files.
Tell us what happened, what you expected, or what would make EEZY DRAW more useful.
You choose the app and recipient. Nothing is sent automatically, and project files are not attached.
